title: Deciphering the charge transport mechanism in different layers of RbGeBr 3 -based perovskite solar cells for sustainable green energy applications
content: Significant scientific attention is directed toward inorganic perovskite-based photovoltaics, a direct result of their extremely high and consistently increasing power conversion efficiencies (PCEs). Lead-free TiO2/rubidium germanium tribromide (RbGeBr3)/spiro-OMeTAD and TiO2/barium zirconium trisulfide (BaZrS3)/spiro-OMeTAD perovskite solar cells were designed and analyzed using COMSOL Multiphysics to investigate their photovoltaic behavior. The simulation results show that device performance is strongly influenced by layer thickness, carrier concentration, and operating temperature. The highest short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 26.48 mA cm−2 was obtained when the RbGeBr3 absorber thickness was increased to 1030 nm, whereas a maximum open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 1.37 V was achieved at a thickness of 280 nm. The optimized structure delivered a fill factor of 73.19% and a PCE of 24.26% with both the electron-transport layer (ETL) and hole-transport layer (HTL) set to 10 nm. The device also maintained strong performance over the investigated temperature range, with efficiency increasing from 20.8% at 250 K to 22.4% at 350 K. TiO2/BaZrS3/spiro-OMeTAD achieved a PCE of 22.11% when acceptor and donor densities vary from 1 × 1014 to 1 × 1018 cm−3. These results demonstrate that careful optimization of structural and electrical parameters can significantly enhance the performance of RbGeBr3-based lead-free perovskite solar cells (PSCs).
